proof_audit.finding: Pass within declared domain. Independent increments are relative to the full named filtration. Gaussian second/fourth moments give L2 variance 2 sum h_i^2; deterministic shrinking meshes give L2/probability convergence. Dyadic summability plus Borel-Cantelli supplies the a.s. set used to contradict finite variation. Rational subintervals extend infinite variation to every positive interval. Brownian existence/usual augmentation are explicitly invoked, not purportedly proved by paths.

proof_audit.topic: Elementary integrals, isometry, completion and predictable density
proof_audit.finding: Pass. Later-increment conditioning eliminates cross terms without falsely assuming holdings independent of earlier increments. Truncation handles unbounded L2 coefficients. Isometry gives a well-defined linear L2-completion and conditional expectation contraction passes martingale identities to the limit. Conditional second moments are justified by event tests. Indicator closure is a sigma-algebra: clipping and finite maxima preserve elementary predictable form on common partitions, countable unions use finite P x dt mass, and predictable simple/truncated approximations complete the identification. Pointwise subsequence limits supply predictable versions modulo P x dt null sets.

proof_audit.topic: Doob L2 bound and continuous version
proof_audit.finding: Pass. Finite-grid first-crossing events lie in the crossing information set; conditional Jensen gives the tail inequality. Integration up to R gives the truncated squared maximum and Cauchy-Schwarz yields factor4. Monotone limits first in R then dense nested grids use continuity. Applying this to elementary integral differences gives expected uniform Cauchy control; a summable subsequence yields uniform a.s. convergence to a continuous version agreeing with each fixed-time L2 limit. No circular assumption of continuity for the newly completed integral.

Pass. Predictable stopped integrands are obtained by finite-grid stops and dyadic approximation from above. Isometry plus continuous integral paths identifies stopped gains. Accumulated-square thresholds make stopped H2 norms finite and compatible. Local zero-drift integrals are not assigned an unconditional zero mean without further integrability.

Pass for the stated continuous-coefficient C1,2 class. Frozen diffusion error sums vanish in L1 by isometry and bounded dominated convergence. Squared finite-variation increments vanish and Cauchy-Schwarz controls cross terms. Bounded predictable random weights retain orthogonality of centered Brownian squares. Riemann sums identify weighted quadratic variation. Splitting time change at the next state needs only f_t continuity; second spatial Taylor remainders are modulus of continuity times tight squared-increment sums. Linear stochastic sums converge in L2. Rational-time identities plus continuity give simultaneous equality.

Pass. Compact state/time cutoffs bound derivatives and continuous adapted coefficients. The author explicitly handles an immediate stop caused by an unbounded initial coefficient and changes only time-zero values; stopped coefficients have at most one discontinuity, so dt-a.e. left approximation and bounded dominated convergence remain available. Evaluating the stopped-process formula at t wedge tau stops its time term too. Open-domain exits and U<T for terminal singularity are explicit. No full semimartingale or merely predictable-coefficient Ito theorem is claimed proved.

Pass. Polarization of quadratic sums and scalar-square Ito identities yields integral b*d for common-driver covariation and the product correction. Deterministic finite-variation factors have zero correction. Portfolio marked value is distinguished from self-financing trading gains; the latter is an additional cash restriction.

proof_audit.topic: GBM existence, pathwise uniqueness and moments
proof_audit.finding: Pass. Explicit exponential is verified with Ito before taking logs. The positive integrating factor is defined from the explicit exponential, so multiplying any competing continuous solution does not presuppose that competitor is positive. Drift and diffusion cancel including cross variation. Log formula is localized away from zero. Gaussian MGF gives real and conditional moments; the exponential drift-adjusted process is a true L2 martingale before applying Doob. Zero initial price, zero diffusion and negative initial sign are treated separately; only the explicit linear SDE receives a uniqueness claim.

Pass. One-step exponential-normal MGF differentiation gives the shared exact/Euler cross moment. Its product across independent increments yields the stated MSE and bias with different units. Three-point cubature matches degree-four moments only and is separated from Gaussian exponential moments. Fixed polygon refinement is explicitly not new Brownian information. Negative Euler values are retained as a scheme failure rather than clipped.

numerical_methods.transforms: Independent Gaussian Simpson integrals on [-12,12] with 8192 panels; finite differences of e^-kt x^2 for generator coefficients; tensor 3-point quadrature for polynomial adapted-integral moments.
numerical_methods.GBM_error: 105-digit per-step moment anchors with MSE=(sqrt(A)-sqrt(B))^2+2(sqrt(A B)-C), distinct from author model A+B-2C; path values composed by per-step transitions.
numerical_methods.tolerances: Ordinary comparisons use 2e-10*max(1,abs(expected)); integrated variances 2e-9; generator finite differences 2e-6 and diffusion 2e-7. Tiny-coefficient probes ensure finite nonnegative behavior but do not claim relative accuracy for vanishing quantities. Exact rational values use equality.
